charles-callet.name: Charles Callet
charles-callet.bio: Charles Callet was a French composer and game musician associated with the French computer-game industry, including work for Infogrames and related studios. His Amiga credits in the CCG archive include Hostages, North & South and Ween: The Prophecy. Published sources disagree over his precise birth year, so it is intentionally omitted here.

charles-deenen.name: Charles Deenen
charles-deenen.bio: Charles Deenen is a Dutch audio director, composer, sound designer and mixer who began experimenting with computer sound as a teenager. He co-founded Maniacs of Noise with Jeroen Tel and contributed to C64 and Amiga game audio before building a long international career in interactive and film sound.

charlie-kellner.name: Charlie Kellner
charlie-kellner.bio: Charlie Kellner is an American programmer and game-audio contributor associated with Lucasfilm Games in the 1980s. His Commodore 64 music credits include Rescue on Fractalus and The Eidolon, alongside earlier work with computer music tools and 6502-based systems.

chris-cox.name: Chris Cox
chris-cox.bio: Chris Cox is an American programmer and musician whose C64 credits include China Miner, Doriath and Tales of the Arabian Nights. His work is associated with the early Interceptor and Orpheus period of British home-computer publishing.

chris-grigg.name: Chris Grigg
chris-grigg.bio: Chris Grigg is an American composer, sound designer and audio programmer whose career includes work for Waveform, Future Arts, Lucasfilm Games and Epyx. His C64 credits in the CCG archive include California Games and Maniac Mansion, and his later career extended into film audio, interactive sound and music technology.

chris-huelsbeck.name: Chris Hülsbeck
chris-huelsbeck.bio: Chris Hülsbeck is a German game composer who began creating music on the Commodore 64 as a teenager. After winning a German computer-magazine music competition he built a career that includes The Great Giana Sisters and the Turrican series, later expanding into console and orchestral game-music projects.

dave-lowe.name: Dave Lowe
dave-lowe.bio: Dave Lowe, also known professionally as Uncle Art, is an English composer and sound designer whose game-audio career spans the 8-bit, 16-bit and console eras. His CCG-linked credits include Power Drift, Double Dragon II and the Amiga version of International Karate, while his wider work covers many more games and formats.

dave-pridmore.name: Dave Pridmore
dave-pridmore.bio: Dave Pridmore is a British game-audio contributor whose recorded credits include work on Jack the Nipper II and Rick Dangerous. Public personal information is limited, so the CCG profile focuses on his documented soundtrack contributions.

dave-thomas.name: Dave Thomas
dave-thomas.bio: Dave Thomas is a British programmer, artist and musician associated with a run of Commodore 64 releases in the mid-1980s. The CCG archive links him to Blackwyche, Dragon Skulle, Entombed, Outlaws, The Staff of Karnath and Buggy Boy, reflecting a multi-discipline role rather than music alone.

sources.title: GameBase64 and historical C64 credit records

dave-warhol.name: Dave Warhol
dave-warhol.bio: Dave Warhol is an American game composer, programmer and producer who worked at Mattel during the Intellivision era before founding Realtime Associates in 1986. His career spans game audio, programming and production across many systems, with C64 credits in the CCG archive including Neuromancer and Heart of Africa.

david-dunn.name: David Dunn
david-dunn.bio: David Dunn is a British game musician and programmer represented in the CCG archive by a group of mid-1980s Commodore 64 titles including Chiller, Elite, Finders Keepers, High Noon and The Trap Door. Surviving public biographical material is sparse, so the profile avoids unsupported birth details.

david-thiel.name: David Thiel
david-thiel.bio: David Thiel is an American composer, sound designer and audio programmer whose game-audio career reaches back to the early arcade industry. He worked at Gottlieb on titles including Q*bert before moving into home-computer and later game-audio development; his CCG-linked credits include Winter Games, Championship Wrestling and The Three Stooges.
